request.spec:
The sheet has a review SLA (settings, days, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED key=review-sla
value=<days>; blank means none). A REVIEW claim whose review day (the sheet's today when it went to
REVIEW) plus the SLA days is before the sheet's today shows review-late yes; the summary counts
such claims.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has a review SLA (settings, days, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED key=review-sla
value=<days>; blank means none). A REVIEW claim whose review day (the sheet's today when it went to
REVIEW) plus the SLA days is before the sheet's today shows review-late yes; the summary counts
such claims.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The review SLA is in place. The main `review sla` test passes. The three scenario tests still fail on the unedited spec, but only because of a bug in the spec itself: each one expects `sheet-parent` to show the literal text `"__SHEET__-p"` (lines 239, 640, 1059) instead of the real sheet id, like `smvkq089h5crq-p`. The app shows the right value there. I ran a throwaway copy of the spec with that placeholder filled in as `` `${sheet}-p` ``, and all four tests passed, so everything else those scenarios check works. I deleted the copy; the real spec is untouched. Someone with access to the spec will need to fix those three lines.

One thing to watch when running it: your shell has `PORT=3002` set, and something else is already using that port. The app couldn't start, so the first run actually tested some other server. Run it on a free port instead, e.g. `PORT=3017 bin/e2e`.

**What changed**
- **Stored data** (`V97__review_sla.sql`): the sheet gets a `review_sla` column (days, blank means none, not dated). Each claim gets a `review_on` date: the sheet's today when the claim goes to REVIEW. It's set in `ClaimRepository.changeStatus`, which also covers bulk open. Cloning a sheet copies both.
- **Settings** (built the same way as the existing escalate-after setting): saving a value checks it's a whole number of days or blank, and writes `SETTING_CHANGED ... key=review-sla value=<days>` to the audit file. The form has a new `setting-review-sla` field and shows the current value in `setting-review-sla-current`.
- **Server response**: the claims list now includes each claim's review day.
- **Screen**: a new `reviewLate` check in `claims.ts` marks a claim as late when it is REVIEW and its review day plus the SLA days is before the sheet's today. Each claim row shows `claim-review-late` as yes/no, and the summary shows `summary-review-late-count`.

Only the claims list returns the review day; responses for a single claim leave it empty. The screen doesn't read those responses (it always re-fetches the list), so nothing is affected today.
